G = nx.Graph()

# Compute a connected dominating set
# Using the greedy algorithm for connected dominating set
# (Note: This is an approximation algorithm)
# https://networkx.org/documentation/stable/reference/algorithms/generated/networkx.algorithms.approximation.clique.max_clique.html
# https://networkx.org/documentation/stable/reference/algorithms/generated/networkx.algorithms.dominating.dominating_set.html

# Function to compute a connected dominating set
# (This is a custom implementation for the purpose of this example)
def connected_dominating_set(G):
    # Start with an empty set
    D = set()
    # Copy the graph to work with
    H = G.copy()
    
    # While there are nodes in the graph
    while H.nodes:
        # Find a node with the highest degree
        node = max(H.nodes, key=lambda n: H.degree[n])
        # Add the node to the dominating set
        D.add(node)
        # Remove the node and its neighbors from the graph
        H.remove_nodes_from(list(H.neighbors(node)) + [node])
    
    return D

# Compute the connected dominating set
D = connected_dominating_set(G)

# Sort the nodes in the dominating set
D_sorted = sorted(D)

# Print the result as a JSON list
print(json.dumps(D_sorted))
